Apple is developing a screen-less health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to the latest report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly "working on prototypes," but has yet to decide whether to ultimately launch the product.

Bloomberg reports that the internally developed prototype features a "slim fabric band with a built-in computing module containing sensors." The project is currently in the "technical exploration" phase, and Bloomberg notes the product won't launch until at least 2028, assuming Apple ultimately decides to bring it to market.

The project is said to have the support of Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October, succeeding the departing Jeff Williams.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who want to track health and fitness without wearing a smartwatch. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing for an IPO and recently disclosed sales of 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue in the nine months ending June 30 grew 74% year-over-year to $1.21 billion.

However, Apple remains the dominant player in the smartwatch market. The Apple Watch also offers far more features than health-and-fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
